MARKET.head: French wine imports to China jump in September on restocking and cheaper 2024 Bordeaux
MARKET.summ: China’s imports of French wine surged in September 2026, with their value rising nearly 130% from August and volume almost doubling
takeaways: China imported 4.44 million litres of French wine worth US$73.69 million in September 2026, up 129.7% in value from August.
Importers credit holiday restocking, cheaper 2024 Bordeaux en primeur prices, and tight stocks of sought-after wines like Carruades de Lafite.
Some importers say the jump reflects restocking rather than a clear recovery in Chinese consumer demand, which remains price-sensitive.

MARKET.head: Changyu partners with South Korea's Ayoung as domestic profits slide
MARKET.summ: With profits down nearly 20% despite rising sales, Changyu has struck a deal with South Korean drinks group Ayoung to put its wines in supermarkets, specialist shops and restaurants and hired a local team to build demand beyond the first shipment
takeaways: Changyu, China's biggest wine producer, signed a strategic deal with South Korean drinks group Ayoung to enter local supermarkets and restaurants.
In the first nine months of 2026, Changyu's revenue rose 6.51% to RMB 2.254 billion while net profit fell 19.25% to RMB 151 million.
South Korea's wine imports fell 3.18% in volume in the first half of 2026, though their value rose 1.71% to US$214.78 million.

MARKET.head: AWRI re-elects two Directors and appoints Steven Weinert to its Board
MARKET.summ: 24 November 2026 The Australian Wine Research Institute (AWRI) has today announced the re-election of Corrina Wright and Brett McClen to its Board, and the … more
takeaways: Corrina Wright and Brett McClen were re-elected to the AWRI Board by Wine Grapes Levy payers, with terms starting 1 January 2027.
Steven Weinert, a former Pernod Ricard and Wine Australia executive, was appointed Director from 1 November 2026 and will chair the Audit Committee.
Trish Giannini and Sarah Courtney left the Board on 31 October 2026, with Courtney resigning to seek a Liberal Party Senate preselection.

MARKET.head: Fungus-resistant grape varieties cut Apulian table grape protection costs 55%
MARKET.summ: Towards Sustainable Viticulture: Cost Savings and Reduced Chemical Use through Fungus-Resistant Grapevine Varieties
takeaways: Galati et al. (2026) found adopting fungus-resistant grapevine varieties in Apulian table grape production cut plant protection costs by 55%.
The same adoption raised Extended Gross Margins by 7%, 8% without reducing gross revenues, according to the study in Wine Economics and Policy.
Fungus-resistant varieties also reduced cost variability, the researchers reported.

MARKET.head: SWR completes benchmarking of 40-plus global wine sustainability standards
MARKET.summ: (5 min read) Over the past three years, SWR has embarked on the mammoth process of benchmarking the more than 40 sustainability standards that exist globally in wine. Mammoth because the documentation of a standard can easily surpass 1500 pages of documents. The rationale for this when we started was simple.
takeaways: SWR has spent three years benchmarking more than 40 global wine sustainability standards, with most of the work now complete.
Its Global Reference Framework now scores standards across 39 topics, and the OIV is using it to revise its definition of wine sustainability.
Packaging and logistics are the most widespread gap, with few standards setting more than cursory requirements, and SWR plans annual reviews and a searchable tool.

MARKET.head: Sonoma regenerative vineyards match conventional farm returns over 30 years
MARKET.summ: Economic viability of regenerative viticulture in Sonoma County, California IVES Technical Review adapted from Herrera et al. 2026
takeaways: A 30-year cost-benefit study compared regenerative and conventional management across four Sonoma County vineyards, published by Herrera et al. in 2026.
Regenerative vineyards, using no-till alleys, compost, cover crops and sheep grazing, returned financial results close to conventional farming when yields were maintained.
Regenerative sites had slightly lower establishment costs but higher annual operating costs, with general labor dominating expenses in both systems.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux holds 41% of traded wine value as Burgundy's share rises
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux claimed 35.7% of traded value. Burgundy and Champagne followed closely behind
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 41% of the week's traded value, extending its lead, with the 2019 and 2020 vintages top-traded.
Burgundy's share rose from 15.7% to 20.8%, with Domaine de la Romanee-Conti and Domaine Leflaive leading by value.
Champagne's share fell from 13.0% to 8.5%, while Tuscany's rose to 11.6%, led by Soldera Case Basse and Sassicaia.

MARKET.head: Burgundy's top estates face tighter supply and sold-out wines in China
MARKET.summ: Some of Burgundy’s most sought-after wines are becoming harder to source in China, importers told Vino Joy News, as smaller harvests and tighter allocations constrain supply
takeaways: Importers say DRC, Leroy, Leflaive and Domaine Gros Frère et Sœur supplies in China tightened from July, with Leflaive entry whites selling out.
Fine West's Wu Xianghua says Leflaive cut 2024-2025 output and China allocations, so shortages reflect less supply, not stronger demand.
Rival merchant Lin Jianbing says supplies are steady and prices for leading Burgundy wines have fallen over the past two years.

MARKET.head: English sparkling wine's US growth meets oversupply and falling grape prices
MARKET.summ: After a decade of rapid growth and rising international recognition, English sparkling wine faces the challenge of turning enthusiasm into sustained sales
takeaways: English wine plantings rose 510 percent from 2005 to 2024, reaching 4,841 hectares, per Wines of Great Britain.
Global English wine exports grew 35 percent from 2023 to 2024, with the US counted among leading markets.
Grape prices fell about 50 percent after the 2023 vintage, reaching historic lows by end of 2025, says Dermot Sugrue.

MARKET.head: Guangdong lychee ice wine sells out online after APEC banquet menu
MARKET.summ: A Guangdong lychee wine became an unexpected online hit after it was served alongside two Changyu wines at the APEC welcome dinner in Shenzhen, with its producer reporting a more than 93,000% jump in revenue at one online store
takeaways: Yueli Lychee Ice Wine, made by Guangzhou ShunChangYuan in Conghua, was served at the APEC welcome dinner in Shenzhen.
Producer Ou said one online store's revenue rose 93,393.10% after the menu circulated, though the comparison period was not specified.
One flagship store logged about 5,000 orders within two hours on November 19, and the producer began emergency restocking.

MARKET.head: DBR Lafite merges China winery and sales under Leo Wang
MARKET.summ: Former Pernod Ricard executive Leo Wang will oversee Domaine de Long Dai and the group’s China sales team as longtime winery chief Charles Treutenaere prepares to leave
takeaways: Domaines Barons de Rothschild Lafite appointed ex-Pernod Ricard executive Leo Wang to run its China winery and sales as one unit.
Wang becomes managing director of Domaine de Long Dai in Shandong and the Chinese market, splitting time between Shanghai and the estate.
Long Dai general manager Charles Treutenaere, nine years at the estate, leaves at year end; he will assist the handover.

MARKET.head: California Table Grape Commission hires Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie to lead North American marketing
MARKET.summ: The California Table Grape Commission has added Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie as its Global Marketing Director for Canada, Mexico, and Central America
takeaways: The California Table Grape Commission hired Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie as Global Marketing Director for Canada, Mexico and Central America.
She was previously CEO of the Center for Produce Safety and international marketing director for American Pistachio Growers.
She will work with importers and retailers to expand promotions and demand for fresh California table grapes.

CULTURE.head: Twelve US sommeliers name the holiday wines they stock up on
CULTURE.summ: There’s no shortage of occasions to pull out a special bottle of wine during this festive time of year. But beyond the rare, allocated Burgundy and coveted Champagne, the unsung heroes of the holiday season are the affordable, crowd-pleasing bottles that you can break out for any gathering. Now is the time to hit the bottle...
takeaways: Twelve sommeliers from across the US were asked which bottles they stock up on for the holidays.
Picks include Cru Beaujolais such as Morgon and Fleurie, and Cava rosé from Spain.
Other picks include traditional-method sparkling wines, Barbera, Dogliani, and Gruet Sauvage from New Mexico.

CULTURE.head: 24 finalists set for 2026 Big Blind League Grand Final in South Australia
CULTURE.summ: The grand finale of Bottle Shock’s 2026 Big Blind League will be held in Gumeracha, South Australia, this December. Last year, a bacteriologist with no wine background beat a room of wine professionals to win the first Big Blind League Grand Final. On Saturday 5 December, Stefan Sancin will defend his title against 23 of South...
takeaways: The Big Blind League is a blind wine tasting run as a sport, with players answering multiple-choice questions on their phones.
The 24 finalists qualified through five Regional Cups or the season ladder, and include a cellar hand and a prosthetic technician.
The Grand Final is on Saturday 5 December in Gumeracha, South Australia, with defending champion Stefan Sancin competing for $5,000.

CULTURE.head: Schloss Johannisberg tops 50 Best Vineyards 2026 ranking, Bodegas Ysios second
CULTURE.summ: The 50 Best Vineyards 2026 has unveiled its annual ranking with Schloss Johannisberg in Rheingau, Germany taking the top spot. The awards ceremony celebrated outstanding vineyards from 15 destinations across six continents, recognising “excellence in wine, hospitality and visitor experience”. Schloss Johannisberg rose to the...
takeaways: The 50 Best Vineyards 2026 ranking, covering 15 destinations, puts Germany's Schloss Johannisberg in Rheingau first, up from second in 2025.
Spain's Bodegas Ysios in Rioja ranks second and Chile's Montes in Colchagua Valley third, with Montes climbing seven places.
Champagne Taittinger rose 39 places from 50 to 11 to win the Highest Climber Award, and Aya Estate in Bulgaria took the inaugural One to Watch Award.

CULTURE.head: Pridham urges grower-led, collaborative Australian wine industry rebuild over 20 years
CULTURE.summ: In the third instalment of his series examining the future of the Australian wine industry, Ben Pridham from Prodham Viticulture in McLaren Vale moves beyond the problems to consider what comes next. Drawing on his own business experience and examples from overseas, he makes the case for regional collaboration, grower-led...
takeaways: Ben Pridham of Pridham Viticulture in McLaren Vale argues for regional collaboration and grower-led decision-making in Australian wine.
He cites Argentina, where Mendoza's grower-inclusive approach produced around 61% of national wine versus under 7% for San Juan.
He points to South Australia's $109 million Wine Industry Transition and Growth Package, including a $100 million loan scheme for unviable vineyards.

CULTURE.head: Sustainability information lifts consumer interest in fungus-resistant PIWI wines
CULTURE.summ: The Effect of Sustainability Information on Consumers' Preferences for Fungus-Resistant Grape Wine
takeaways: A study tested how sustainability information affects consumer preference and willingness to pay for PIWI (fungus-resistant grape) wine.
Its authors argue wineries should communicate sustainability clearly, since informed buyers drive interest and boost product value.
Separately, a 2026 Agronomy review by Poni et al. covers tools for vineyard resilience under dry-farming conditions.

CULTURE.head: ProWine Shanghai shows China's wine buyers seeking distinctive, regional, casual wines
CULTURE.summ: China’s wine market is becoming more selective, more diverse and less dependent on formal drinking occasions, according to exhibitors at this year’s ProWine Shanghai
takeaways: ProWine Shanghai drew 620-plus exhibitors from 34 countries and regions and 21,800 trade visitors over three days.
Chinese buyers are becoming more selective, seeking wines with distinctive character beyond quality and price, per Wines of Portugal's Frederico Falcão.
Wine drinking is widening beyond business banquets and gifting into casual restaurants, wine bars and drinking at home.

CULTURE.head: VinePair names 20 Proseccos to buy in 2026, tasted without blind conditions
CULTURE.summ: Prosecco continues to be a bright spot for the wine industry, as the Italian sparkling wine manages to keep growing year after year. Between the thirst for affordable bubbly and the unstoppable rise of the Spritz category, it’s no wonder more consumers are looking to this budget-friendly style. Even though the standard DOC...
takeaways: VinePair's 2026 roundup lists 20 Proseccos, scored on a 100-point scale for aromas, flavors, texture and finish.
Producers and PR firms sent samples free of charge, and tastings were not blind, with price and producer known.
The list also weighs quality, price and availability, with several bottles under $15 or $20 highlighted.

SCIENCE.head: Biochar in vineyard soils: review weighs yield gains and carbon capture
SCIENCE.summ: The use of biochar in agricultural soils: Impacts on vineyard productivity and the potential for carbon capture and sequestration
takeaways: Leonel J.R. Nunes published a study on biochar use in agricultural soils in Science of The Total Environment, November 2026.
The paper assesses biochar's impacts on vineyard productivity and its potential for carbon capture and sequestration.

SCIENCE.head: Review assesses tools for keeping vineyards resilient under dry-farming water stress
SCIENCE.summ: The study provides a narrative and critical literature review evaluating the physiological, agronomic, and practical tools available to enhance vineyard resilience under dry-farming conditions, and analyzes grapevine strategies for managing water stress. Published by Poni et al 2026 in Agronomy, MDPI Headline Findings Results
takeaways: Poni and colleagues, writing in the journal Agronomy in 2026, reviewed tools for vineyard resilience under dry-farming conditions.
The review evaluates physiological and agronomic strategies grapevines use to manage water stress.
Coverage also cites a study pairing winter-spring cover crops with a foliar nitrogen-fixing biostimulant in rainfed vineyards.

SCIENCE.head: Cover crops plus foliar biostimulant match tilled Syrah yields in Spain
SCIENCE.summ: Pairing winter-spring cover crops with a foliar nitrogen-fixing microbial biostimulant supports sustainable rainfed viticulture through complementary soil and plant pathways, boosting soil nutrient enzymes while keeping yields and juice traits competitive or improved
takeaways: A two-year 2020-2021 trial in rainfed organic Syrah vines in southern Spain compared tillage with winter-spring cover crops.
Cover crops raised soil nutrient enzyme activity, and high-dose Methylobacterium biostimulant plus cover crops matched or beat tilled yields.
The combination also showed a possible synergy in juice °Brix and pH, per the study published in Soil and Tillage Research.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Schloss Vaux: this leading German sparkling wine house has a new home on the Rhein
NEWSLETTERS.summ: I visited Vaux, one of Germany’s leading sparkling wine houses, in August 2026. They took a group of press to
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Schloss Vaux has opened VAUX am Rhein, a new visitor venue in a 12th-century riverside fortress in Eltville, Rheingau, led by sommelier Florian Richter.
Vaux produces about 450,000 bottles of traditional-method sparkling wine annually, sourcing from its own vineyards (since 2014) and from the Rheingau, Pfalz and Nahe.
Vaux has no reserve wine programme, so almost all its wines are vintage, and its style emphasises fruit rather than bone-dry austerity.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Inside This Year’s Hospices de Beaune Auction: The Drama, the Records and the Wines That Found Their Buyers
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Discover the drama and record-breaking moments from this iconic Burgundy charity wine auction, featuring exceptional barrels and the buyers who claimed them
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: The 2026 Hospices de Beaune auction raised €14.4 million at the hammer, down from €18.8 million in 2025, with 348 red and 86 white barrels offered.
Red barrels averaged €28,931, up 5 per cent, while white barrels averaged €39,893, down from €58,580, a fall of almost a third.
The Clos de Vougeot Grand Cru charity barrel sold for €770,000 to Alaor Pereira Lino of Anima Vinum, with the Faiveley family's extra €230,000 bringing the total to €1 million.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Wine News: What I’m Reading the Week of 11/22/26
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly roundup of the wine stories that I find of interest on the web. I
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: Beaujolais Anew
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The 2026 release of that wine we love to hate and hate to love, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Beaujolais Nouveau was pushed onto the world stage by Beaujolais vignerons, with Georges Duboeuf marketing it beyond French borders by the 1970s.
Beaujolais Nouveau is released worldwide on the third Thursday of November, and wines from crus like Morgon cannot carry the Beaujolais Nouveau label.
Marcel Lapierre, in Morgon, labels his new red as a Vin de France with the nickname "Raisins Gaulois" due to French labeling rules.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Cabernet Franc in the Press: November 2026
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Livermore wins Region of the Year, Wine Spectator profiles Loire Cabernet Franc, Decanter takes a cross-border look at Ontario and New York, and much more
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Wine Enthusiast named California's Livermore Valley its 2026 American Wine Region of the Year in its annual Wine Star Awards.
Livermore Valley is known for Sauvignon Blanc and Cabernet Franc, which the regional association named its signature white and red varieties in February 2025.
A Cabernet Franc claimed top honours at Maryland's Governor's Cup, per the newsletter.

NEWSLETTERS.head: More Than Skin Deep: A Grape with a Colourful Past
NEWSLETTERS.summ: A colourful tale of the grape that was born to dye and the father-son team behind it
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier, Champagne's black grapes, have colourless juice, so they can make white 'Blanc de Noirs' Champagne.
Garnacha Tintorera, also called Alicante Bouschet, is a red-fleshed grape bred in the late 1800s by Henri Bouschet from Petit Bouschet and Garnacha Tinto.
Henry Jeffreys reported that a top Burgundy producer reportedly grows Alicante Bouschet to boost the colour of his Pinot Noir.

NEWSLETTERS.head: What the Hell Do They Mean?
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Let’s play wine tasting note bingo, here’s TMC’s handy guide
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Tasting-note term 'minerality' is described as a mysterious, widely used descriptor with little agreed meaning, often used when a writer has nothing specific to say.
'Vertical cohesiveness' is cited as a phrase that can safely be applied to any wine, sometimes combined with other terms like 'vertical minerality'.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Many Sins Of Wine Critics
NEWSLETTERS.summ: In the exciting (other adjectives are available) times we’re living in, we’re often told that writing is passé, people just don’t bother reading words anymore. A few journalistic outlets, especially in the financial press, seem to have finally come clean about the seriousness of their reporting, by auto-summarising their pieces...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues wine critics should know slightly more than their target audience, rather than being supertasters or superior experts.
Atkin says the American critic model favours tasting ability while the British model favours theoretical knowledge and scholarship.
Atkin criticises the roughly 30-second tasting ritual, often applied to tens or over a hundred wines, as an inadequate basis for judging wine.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Find Rare Shizz With Orpheus Alerts!
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Some (more!) exciting news, folks: As many of you already know, sometimes wines get featured on here that are pretty rare. I’m talking about the kind of stuff that either doesn’t make it to the big platforms, or, if it does, is either priced astronomically or is gone in milliseconds. Understandably, that can be somewhat […]...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude is partnering with Orpheus Alerts, part of Orpheus Intelligence Labs Inc., to help buyers find rare wines.
Orpheus monitors sources such as local-language catalogues, merchant inventories, auction and consignment notices, and private cellar sales.
Users create alerts using natural-language descriptions or images, and Orpheus notifies them when matching wine is available in its network and connects them with sellers.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing, with Guangzhou scheduled for November 6.
Spain ranked fifth by volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy but a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
DCOOP's Airén and Tempranillo, plus Ayuso and Campos Reales Verdejo, were highlighted as entry-level wines priced around RMB12 to RMB24 export.
